claims.claim: Smaller vowel space predicts more reduction only when articulation rate is included; rate is the strongest predictor and VDI is not significant.
claims.limitations: The French speakers, spontaneous tasks, reduction definition, and acoustic measures bound the result; other languages and conversational settings remain open.

claims.claim: Advanced learners improve, especially for /i-I/; formant movement increases with proficiency, while length of residence is not significant.
claims.limitations: The learner group, contrasts, language experience, and measurements bound the result; other L1s and natural interaction need separate evidence.

claims.claim: The paper reports a 30x smaller network, a further halving of neural cost with one-hop latency, and orders-of-magnitude solver speedup while retaining quality.
claims.limitations: Spectrogram settings, audio domain, latency definition, and samples bound the claim; listening tests and hardware deployment remain separate checks.

claims.claim: Self-adaptors align with longer pauses, utterance-final syntax shortens pauses, and most gestured pauses occur within utterances.
claims.limitations: Corpus annotation, participant population, gesture categories, and observational design bound the result; causal cognitive interpretations remain hypotheses.

claims.claim: The paper presents a reference-free evaluation framework for meeting summarization and reports its ability to rank systems/prompts.
claims.limitations: Facts, judge prompts, meeting domain, and pairwise comparison protocol bound the result; human validation and adversarial summaries remain open.

claims.claim: The paper reports improved prediction performance and robustness on both tasks.
claims.limitations: Listener panels, rating prompts, comparison construction, and datasets bound the result; agreement and usefulness for new listener populations remain open.

claims.claim: HEGP predicts effort similarly across styles; wider F0 range and slower articulation are associated with lower effort, especially for habitual speech.
claims.limitations: Noise, listener ratings, speech styles, and HEGP definition bound the result; individual strategy and real device conditions remain open.

claims.claim: The paper reports more than 40% relative reduction in biased WER from ranking and selection.
claims.limitations: NER list, LibriSpeech, Whisper context mechanism, and bias-word definition bound the result; new domains and errors in entity extraction remain open.
